item.mechanism: Lower annealing temperature reduces configurational entropy stability, driving the single ordered B2 phase to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution.
item.supporting_observation: APT results revealed fine scale precipitate-like regions rich in Fe and Co within an Al-Ni rich B2 matrix, characterized as a B2 + BCC decomposition.
item.scope_limits: At 1000 °C, the same alloy remains a single phase B2; the mechanism is weak at lower temperatures compared to Cr-substituted alloys.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors note that while SEM showed a single phase, finer scale separation was only revealed by TEM and APT, ruling out a purely single-phase structure at this scale.
quotes: lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution.
Fine scale precipitate-like regions rich in Fe and Co were observed, the matrix is rich in Al and Ni.
reducing the temperature to 600 °C induces the early stages of phase separation into B2 + BCC

records.text: Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Lower annealing temperature reduces configurational entropy stability, driving the single ordered B2 phase to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution.. System: AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy. Conditions: Annealed at 600 °C for 15 h. Evidence: measured. Observation: APT results revealed fine scale precipitate-like regions rich in Fe and Co within an Al-Ni rich B2 matrix, characterized as a B2 + BCC decomposition.. Scope limits: At 1000 °C, the same alloy remains a single phase B2; the mechanism is weak at lower temperatures compared to Cr-substituted alloys.. Alternatives: The authors note that while SEM showed a single phase, finer scale separation was only revealed by TEM and APT, ruling out a purely single-phase structure at this scale.. Quote: "lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution."

item.mechanism: Substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr introduces positive enthalpies of mixing (Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, Ni-Cr), creating miscibility gaps that strongly enhance the tendency for B2 phase decomposition.
item.supporting_observation: The addition of Cr caused a strong tendency for phase separation into B2 + BCC even at 1000 °C, unlike the Cr-free alloy.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism does not apply to the Al-Cr binary system which has a propensity for compound formation due to negative enthalpy of mixing.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors considered that the phase separation is introduced by Cr, distinct from the behavior of AlCoFeNi.
quotes: The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems
Addition of Cr strongly enhances the tendency of the B2 phase to decompose into a B2 + BCC mixture
In all, it appears that the phase separation tendency in the current HEA is introduced by Cr.

item.mechanism: Annealing temperature controls the length scale of phase decomposition, with lower temperatures promoting finer, hierarchical precipitation (nanometer scale) compared to coarser decomposition at higher temperatures.
item.supporting_observation: 600 °C annealing resulted in multiple length scales (~50–100 nm and ~3–5 nm), while 1000 °C resulted in micron-scale decomposition.
item.scope_limits: This hierarchical effect is specific to the Cr-substituted alloy; the Cr-free alloy shows only early stage separation at 600 °C.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors distinguish between the coarse decomposition at 1000 °C and the refined scale at 600 °C.
quotes: The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature
A coarse length scale of decomposition is observed in the case of the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy after 1000 °C/15 hrs annealing
a substantially refined length scale of decomposition is observed in the case of the same alloy after annealing at 600 °C/15 h.

item.mechanism: The presence of a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure increases microhardness through microstructural refinement and phase boundary strengthening compared to a single-phase B2 matrix.
item.system: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi high entropy alloys
item.supporting_observation: The hierarchically decomposed B2 + BCC microstructure in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi at 600 °C showed the highest hardness (475 VHN) compared to the single phase B2 at 1000 °C (406 VHN).
item.scope_limits: The mechanism relies on the extent of decomposition; the Cr-free alloy at 600 °C also showed high hardness despite early stage decomposition.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors attribute the hardness difference to the phase state (single vs multi-phase) rather than just grain size.
quotes: The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.
the single phase B2 microstructure has a lower hardness as compared to the hierarchically decomposed B2 + BCC microstructure.
the 600 °C annealed condition of the AlCoFeNi alloy also exhibits a very high microhardness of 474 VHN, despite the fact that only an early stage of phase decomposition into B2 + BCC was exhibited

item.mechanism: The antiferromagnetic nature of Cr reduces the overall saturation magnetization of the alloy by diluting the ferromagnetic moments of Co and Fe.
item.supporting_observation: Saturation magnetization (Ms) dropped by more than 50% in the Cr-containing alloy compared to the Cr-free alloy.
item.scope_limits: This effect is specific to the addition of Cr; the Cr-free alloy maintains high Ms.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors note that while Cr is detrimental to soft magnetic properties, it benefits corrosion resistance.
quotes: replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization
It has been previously reported earlier that M S falls linearly with increasing Cr content
This is mainly due to the antiferromagnetic nature of Cr.

item.mechanism: Nanoscale phase decomposition into ferromagnetic (Fe-Co rich) and antiferromagnetic (Cr rich) regions creates pinning sites that increase coercivity.
item.system: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi high entropy alloys
item.supporting_observation: Coercivity increased from 4.3 Oe (1000 °C, homogeneous) to 14.5 Oe (600 °C, nanoscale separation) in AlCoFeNi, and was significantly higher in Cr-containing alloys.
item.scope_limits: The exact relationship between B2 decomposition and coercivity is noted as not well understood and requiring further investigation.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors mention that coercivity can also be affected by impurities, deformation, and grain size.
quotes: The coercivity ( H c ) decreased with increasing annealing temperature from 15 Oe for sample aged at 600 °C/15 h, exhibiting nanoscale phase separation, to 4 Oe for samples aged at 1000 °C/15 h, exhibiting a homogeneous undecomposed B2 matrix.
magnetic hardening of Fe–Co–Cr alloys is associated with the formation of a two-phase microstructure at the nanometer scale
The relationship between the decomposition of the B2 phase into a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure and the resulting coercivity is not well understood

item.mechanism: Thermodynamic nucleation barriers due to high interfacial energy can kinetically inhibit the precipitation of equilibrium phases (like FCC) even when thermodynamically predicted.
item.supporting_observation: CALPHAD predicted FCC phase at 1000 °C, but experimental observations showed only B2, suggesting sluggish kinetics.
item.scope_limits: This kinetic inhibition might be overcome at high energy sites like high angle grain boundaries.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors suggest FCC precipitation could be limited solely to high angle grain boundaries.
quotes: Note that there is likely to be a high thermodynamic nucleation barrier for the precipitation of the FCC phase within the B2 matrix owing to the high interfacial energy between these two phases
Consequently, the kinetics of precipitation could be extremely sluggish, and FCC precipitation could be limited solely to high angle grain boundaries which are high energy sites.
However, in the experimental observations, there was no conclusive FCC formation observed in case of the AlCoFeNi 1000 °C/15 h annealed sample.

item.mechanism: The formation of an intermetallic sigma phase at grain boundaries is driven by high local Cr concentration and specific thermodynamic stability in Cr-rich regions.
item.supporting_observation: SADP from grain boundary regions with high Cr concentration was indexed as the sigma phase, distinct from the B2/BCC matrix.
item.scope_limits: The sigma phase was observed at grain boundaries, not within the grain interiors in the APT samples.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors note this phase is often reported in Cr rich steels and HEAs.
quotes: A region with high Cr concentration was also detected near the grain boundaries
The SADP from this grain boundary phase can be consistently indexed as the [001] zone axis of the σ phase
